title: Hold the split lock across the layout read and the pane split
action: Serialize the pane split in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/herding/run.rs so concurrent spawns stop all splitting `right`. The bug, live 2026-08-21: five parallel spawns from one tab all right-split (panes p3R p3S p3T p3V p3W) and worker 5 died on the 180s ack-wait budget, because every process read a stale layout showing pane_count 1. Find the region with `rg -n 'pane_current|pane_layout|resolve_split_parent|tab_create' packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/herding/run.rs`; the guarded region is the run of statements starting at `let own_pane = match herdr.pane_current()` and ending when `new_pane` is bound - it currently reads `let layout = herdr.pane_layout(&own_pane);`, then `let parent = resolve_split_parent(layout.as_deref(), &own_pane);`, then the `match parent.refusal` arms that call `herdr.pane_split(...)` or, on the hps-13 width refusal, `herdr.tab_create(...)`. Extract that whole run into one helper function taking the herdr, own_pane/cwd/job_id and the main root, so the lock's scope is the helper body and the guard drops the moment the new pane exists. Acquire with herding::split_lock::acquire(&opts.main_root, &opts.job_id, <budget>) at the top of the helper - a budget generous enough that a queued spawn waits rather than fails (the ack-wait budget is 180s; 120s is the intended value). Fail OPEN, matching the fail-open habit this file already uses for the layout read and the hps-8 workspace-trust pre-flight: on Ok(None) (budget spent) or Err, print an eprintln! warning naming the lock and proceed with the split anyway - a spawn that never happens is worse than a mis-directed one. Keep every existing behavior inside the region byte-for-byte otherwise: the hps-8 pre-flight stays BEFORE the lock, the hps-13 fresh-tab fallback stays inside it, resolve_split_parent and split_direction are untouched, and every existing SpawnFailed message keeps its wording. Regression test in run.rs's existing #[cfg(test)] block, alongside the existing fake-Herdr test doubles (`rg -n 'fn pane_layout' packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/herding/run.rs` finds them): a fake Herdr whose pane list lives behind a shared Mutex, where pane_split PUSHES the new pane into that list and pane_layout returns the current list; drive the helper from two threads against one temp main root and assert the two recorded split directions are `right` then `down`, never `right` twice - the exact regression. Keep the fake's pane_split slow enough (a short sleep before the push) that an unlocked implementation reliably fails the test.

truths: Two concurrent spawns from one tab produce one right split and one down split, never two right splits
A lock that cannot be taken within the budget warns and still spawns

deviations: split_worker_pane takes the acquire budget as a parameter; the one production call site passes the SPLIT_LOCK_WAIT const (120s). The seam makes the budget-spent fail-open branch provable in a millisecond test instead of a two-minute one.

Reserved and edited split_lock.rs as well: run.rs now calls acquire, so the module-level allow(dead_code) was stale. Removed it and narrowed the opt-out to SplitLock::path(), the one item still test-only, with its own reason comment.
Negative check run and reverted: with acquire replaced by Ok(None), the regression test records [right, right] and fails, so the test really catches the bug.
